title: Impact of Singapore Bank Loans to Coal Power Projects on Government's Carbon Emission Commitments
what_it_is: Impact of Singapore Bank Loans to Coal Power Projects on Government's Carbon Emission Commitments

sections.label: Banks financing coal power projects
sections.summary: Local banks' financing of coal power projects must be understood in the context of rapidly growing regional energy needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The local banks' financing of coal power projects has to be understood, firstly, in the context of rapidly growing energy needs in the region.

sections.label: Banks reviewing customer portfolios
sections.summary: Local banks are expected to complete the review of their entire customer portfolios by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The local banks are expected to complete the review of their entire customer portfolios by the end of this year.

sections.label: DBS pledge and MAS assessments
sections.summary: DBS pledged to stop financing new greenfield coal-fired power projects in OECD and developed markets, and MAS includes banks' sustainability practices in supervisory assessments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) has recently pledged that it will stop financing new greenfield coal-fired power generation projects in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development and developed markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has also included banks' sustainability practices in its supervisory assessments of banks.

sections.label: Banks pledging to move from coal
sections.summary: Banks are pledging to move away from financing coal-powered plants because the opportunities are in renewables.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As a result, we do see banks pledging to move away from financing coal-powered plants, because the opportunities are in renewables.

sections.label: ESG risks and green financing steps
sections.summary: Steps are being taken for banks and MAS to recognise ESG risks, including deeper ESG integration, more green finance products, and building sustainability skills and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On one hand, as I mentioned earlier in my reply, more steps are being taken for our banks, as well as MAS, to recognise the ESG risks in all these projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Some of these include, first, pushing for deeper ESG integration in our finance institutions (FIs); second, expanding the breadth and depth of green finance products, foster the growth of even the green asset class in Singapore and in the region; and third, deepening research and development and ESG products, building sustainability skills and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, it is really two sides – recognising the risks but, at the same time, building up the ecosystem for green financing.
